subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should non-loopback plain-HTTP browser Control UI sessions be allowed to create and use device identity, or should HTTPS/localhost remain the supported security boundary?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally require a secure browser context for device identity, while the requested change would alter remote browser auth behavior and the threat model for self-hosted LAN deployments.

options.title: Keep Secure Context Default
options.body: Maintain the current HTTPS/localhost requirement and resolve the remaining user pain through warnings, docs, Tailscale/trusted-proxy guidance, and the existing break-glass flag.

options.title: Allow Plain-HTTP Identity
options.body: Permit pure-JS device identity on remote HTTP with explicit docs, dependency review, gateway/UI regression tests, and security copy that explains LAN MitM tradeoffs.

options.title: Add Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the default secure but add a narrowly named operator opt-in for remote HTTP device identity if maintainers want a supported self-hosted LAN exception.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure Context Default
recommendation.body: Maintain the current HTTPS/localhost requirement and resolve the remaining user pain through warnings, docs, Tailscale/trusted-proxy guidance, and the existing break-glass flag.
